title: main-sync git-merge-main uses --no-ff so a diverged branch can sync, and its failure path is transactional

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Last commit on this branch touching a non-proof path (round-6 remediation). merge_sha is null pre-merge as the shared evidence schema requires.

verified_source_sha_history.superseded_reason: Round-1 head. Superseded by the P1 remediation commit: the --no-ff change made a conflicting merge reachable, and the wrapper failure path popped the lane-state autostash and released the merge mutex while MERGE_HEAD and unmerged index entries were still in the worktree.

Round-2 head. Superseded by the round-3 remediation commit: independent review found that abortInProgressSync collapsed an undeterminable probe result into 'the ref is absent', so a repository that could not answer took the 'nothing to abort' early return and the wrapper popped the autostash and released the mutex anyway -- the same fail-open class as the P1, one layer down; and that the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook was called unguarded, so a throwing hook escaped runMergeWrapper with the lock held and no structured result.

Round-3 head. Superseded by the round-4 remediation commit: an independent reviewer demonstrated that the round-3 proof asserted the fail-closed message 'names the git command that actually ran' when commandVector rendered the bridged `git pull --ff-only origin main` instead -- a command that cannot leave MERGE_HEAD behind -- and that three further controls (the abort verb, the not-attempted stash pop, and the unmerged-paths term of the early return) were pinned by no test or mutant.

Round-4 head. Superseded by the round-5 remediation commit: an independent reviewer demonstrated by execution a fail-open that this bundle certified as impossible -- after a SUCCESSFUL merge, a conflicting `git stash pop` leaves unmerged index entries and conflict markers and the wrapper released the merge mutex anyway -- plus an unpinned third term of `residue` (an undeterminable POST-abort state read clean), and three mutation rows (M1/M2/M3) carried forward from round 3 while corroboration claimed all twelve were measured against the current source.

verified_source_sha_history.note: round-6 remediation: measured release decisions, stash-push fail-closed, head-move notice reachability

verdict.mutex_acquire_release_preserved: QUALIFIED — the safety invariant is preserved; the release SITE is deliberately moved by this lane. Round 5 recorded this as a flat true while round 5 was itself relocating the release, and round 6 recorded it as flat true while a stash-push failure still released over a conflicted index. It is now: released after a successful merge, after a cleanly-aborted failing one, and after a non-conflicting pop failure over a MEASURED-clean tree; retained on cleanup failure, on a conflicting pop, on a stash-push failure over an in-progress merge, and whenever the tree could not be measured. Tests 27, 48, 49, 51, 52, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59.
verdict.head_move_invalidation_reporting_preserv: QUALIFIED — the reporting primitives are untouched, but this lane created a path that reached the post-sync analysis with ok:false after a COMMITTED merge (merge_wrapper_stash_pop_conflict), and the `!result.ok` early return skipped both classifyDroppedPaths and renderHeadMoveNotice on it. Reachability repaired in round 6: a failed result keeps its code and the notice is appended to its stderr. Test 57, mutant M18.
verdict.statement: git-merge-main built `git merge --ff-only origin/main`, which cannot merge a diverged branch by definition, so main-sync's recommended exit for divergence failed on exactly the condition it exists for -- leaving git-rebase-main, which rewrites history and invalidates every head-pinned governance artifact, as the only operable path. The command is now `git merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`: it merges a genuinely diverged branch while preserving both sides' commit SHAs byte-for-byte, is deliberately not a bare `git merge` (which would fast-forward a merely-behind branch and make the verb's effect depend on divergence state), and is noninteractive. Permitting a non-fast-forward merge also permits a conflicting one, which exposed a second defect on the same path and was raised as a review P1: the wrapper popped its lane-state autostash and released the merge mutex while MERGE_HEAD and unmerged index entries were still present, stranding lane state in the stash and letting the next lane acquire a mutex over a half-merged worktree. The failure path is now transactional: abortInProgressSync aborts the in-progress merge/rebase and verifies the result before the stash is restored and before the lock is released, and a cleanup that cannot restore the pre-attempt state fails closed with the distinct merge_wrapper_cleanup_failed code, the mutex retained and the stash left intact. All five wrapper safety invariants are preserved; the mutex ordering is hardened, not weakened. Round 3 closed two fail-open residuals found by independent review: an undeterminable probe result (git exit 128) was being read as 'the ref is absent', which sent an unreadable repository down the 'nothing to abort' early return; and the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook was called unguarded, so a throwing hook escaped runMergeWrapper with the lock held and no structured result. Both now force the fail-closed branch. The fail-closed recovery message also named `pnpm ops:merge-wrapper guard`, which only asserts the lock is held; it now names `pnpm ops:merge-lock release`. Round 4 corrected a FALSE claim that round 3's proof made and three controls that nothing pinned, all found by a second independent reviewer. The false claim: the fail-closed message was asserted to name the git command that actually ran, but commandVector was built from the bridged input, so it rendered `git pull --ff-only origin main` -- an invocation that cannot leave MERGE_HEAD behind -- and pointed the operator away from the residue. runMergeWrapper now takes a reportedCommand option: what is run is still `command`, what is reported is the caller's real vector. The three unpinned controls were the abort verb (hardcoding `merge` survived the whole suite; `git merge --abort` during a rebase exits 128 and the residue survives), the not-attempted autostash pop (test 49's assertions were satisfied by git's own refusal to pop into an unmerged index, not by the control), and the unmerged-paths term of the nothing-to-abort early return. Each is now pinned by a test and a mutant (M9-M12). Round 5 closed a fail-open that round 4's proof certified as impossible. Every prior regression entered through the command FAILURE path; this one enters through the SUCCESS path -- the merge completes, `git stash pop` then conflicts because the commit just merged from main touches an autostashed path, and the wrapper released the serializing mutex over a worktree carrying unmerged entries and conflict markers. The release now happens after that branch and the branch returns without releasing. Round 5 also pinned the third term of `residue` (an undeterminable POST-abort state was read as clean, killed by nothing until M13) and re-measured every mutation row: M1/M2/M3 had been carried forward from round 3 at 7/3/5 while the suite grew, and are 10/4/8 against the current source.
verdict.mutex_released_only_after_cleanup_succee: Round 4 asserted this true while a counterexample existed on the SUCCESS path: a conflicting autostash pop left unmerged entries and the mutex was released anyway. Round 5 fixed the code, so the field is true as of 9162d2c9 -- but it was certified before it was proven, and that is recorded in finding 11 rather than quietly corrected.

mutants.name: the mutex released on a conflicting autostash pop

invariants_preserved: merge mutex acquisition and release -- asserted released on the success path, on the cleanly-aborted failure path, and (round 6) after a non-conflicting autostash pop failure over a MEASURED-clean tree; asserted RETAINED on the cleanup-failure path, on an unverifiable post-abort state, on a conflicting autostash pop after a successful merge (round 5), on a stash-PUSH failure over an in-progress merge (round 6), and whenever the worktree could not be measured at all. The round-4 bundle certified the conflicting-pop case impossible and it was not (finding 11); the round-5 bundle then retained the lock on EVERY failed pop, which leaked it over clean trees (finding 12). The invariant is about safety, not about the release site, which this lane deliberately moves.
no history rewriting (parent SHAs asserted byte-for-byte)
protected proof/manifest dropped-path refusal (PROTECTED_SYNC_PATH_PREFIXES / classifyDroppedPaths untouched, outside buildExtendedCommand)

head-move invalidation reporting -- buildHeadMoveInvalidation / renderHeadMoveNotice / HEAD_MOVE_REAUTHORIZATION_ORDER are untouched, AND their reachability was repaired in round 6: this lane created a path (merge_wrapper_stash_pop_conflict) that reaches the post-sync analysis with ok:false after the merge has already been committed, and the `!result.ok` early return silently skipped both the notice and classifyDroppedPaths on it. Test 57, mutant M18.
actionable failure behaviour (conflict diagnostic asserted on both failure paths)
main-sync's merge_wrapper_diverged_requires_explicit_sync refusal is retained; no automatic rebase substitution is restored
no other operation receives the cleanup hook; pr-merge, main-sync and the deferred path have unchanged call sequences, and merge-wrapper.test.ts passes 21/21 unmodified

an undeterminable repository state is never reported clean: `git rev-parse --verify --quiet` exit 1 (absent) and exit 128 (unanswerable) are distinguished, and the second always forces the fail-closed branch
the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook cannot escape runMergeWrapper: a throw becomes the fail-closed result rather than an unwind with the lock held

the reported command is the invocation that actually ran: `reportedCommand` carries the real vector through the main-sync bridge, so result.command and the fail-closed message never name `git pull --ff-only origin main` for a merge or rebase
the abort verb follows the operation, pinned by a real conflicted rebase rather than a mock
an unverifiable POST-abort state is never reported clean: `residue` fails closed on `after.undetermined` as well as on surviving refs and unmerged paths

release decisions are MEASUREMENTS, not assumptions: worktreeResidue probes MERGE_HEAD, REBASE_HEAD and `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` after a failed stash push or pop, and the operator-facing message reports what it found rather than asserting a conflict the code never observed
an UNMEASURED worktree is never treated as a clean one: with no residueProbe supplied, or if the probe throws, measureResidue returns not-clean and the mutex is retained (test 59, mutant M19)
scope_refusals: scripts/ops/merge-wrapper.ts was added to file_scope_lock for the P1 remediation only: the stash pop and the mutex release live there and nowhere else, and correcting the ordering elsewhere would have required re-acquiring a released lock, which is racy. One new optional option, one new result code, one guarded early return.
The dual-root sync-contract persistence defect in scripts/ops/codex-exec.ts was NOT bundled into this blocker fix.
The CPU/RAM scheduling contention observed during E2E runs was NOT bundled into this blocker fix.
No package.json, lockfile, tsconfig or build-config change. No workflow, branch-protection, proof-schema or bypass-flag change.
Four --ff-only occurrences belonging to main-sync's legitimate `git pull --ff-only origin main` were deliberately left unchanged.
known_gaps: A merge that conflicts still requires manual resolution by the operator. The wrapper now leaves the worktree exactly as it found it and reports actionably, but it does not resolve the conflict.

A --no-ff merge advances the branch head by one merge commit, which still moves the PR head SHA and therefore still invalidates head-pinned governance artifacts. This lane makes the sanctioned exit operable and SHA-preserving for existing commits; it does not eliminate re-authorization after a sync.
The cleanup-failure path deliberately leaves the mutex held. Recovery is manual and the message says so; there is no automatic lock expiry short of the lock TTL.
--no-edit is pinned by command-shape assertions only (see mutation M2); it cannot be made behaviourally load-bearing under piped stdio.

Rounds 2, 3 and 4 each installed the next defect, and two of the four found in round 4 were proof-integrity failures rather than product failures: a claim with no test behind it, and an assertion that could not fail. Recorded because the pattern is the finding.

`abortInProgressSync` returns an `aborted` field that no caller reads -- `runMergeWrapper` branches on `cleaned` alone. It is dead and pinned by nothing. Left in place rather than removed to keep the round-5 diff to the defects under review; recorded here so it is not mistaken for a control.

Rounds 2, 3, 4 and 5 each installed the next defect. Two of the four found in round 4 and two of the four found in round 5 were proof-integrity failures rather than product failures: claims with no test behind them, assertions that could not fail, and measurements carried forward instead of retaken. That pattern is the durable finding of this lane.

Four consecutive review rounds each found a defect the previous round installed, and three of them found at least one claim the PROOF asserted rather than something the code did. Round 5's fix (retain the mutex on any failed pop) was itself round 6's P1 (a lock leak), and the two are literally each other's mutant (M14/M15). The durable lesson recorded here: a control changed under review pressure needs a mutant in the OPPOSITE direction, or the next round finds it.
